audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 21, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal legal, land-tenure, and reception-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for ancestral land rights, royal purchase pressure, Ahab's entitlement, Jezebel's forged letters, religious fast as legal theater, false witnesses, capital punishment, state murder, land seizure, prophetic confrontation, corpse desecration, misogynistic scapegoating, repentance, restitution, and intergenerational punishment.

verses.restored: After these matters, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel beside palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, Give me your vineyard so it may be for me a vegetable garden, because it is near my house. I will give you in its place a better vineyard, or if good in your eyes, I will give you its price in silver.
Naboth said to Ahab, Far be it from me by YHWH that I give inheritance of my ancestors to you.
Ahab came to his house sullen and angry because of word Naboth the Jezreelite spoke: I will not give you inheritance of my ancestors. He lay upon bed, turned away his face, and ate no bread.
Jezebel his wife came to him and said, Why is your spirit sullen, and why do you not eat bread?

He said to her, Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said, Give me your vineyard for silver, or if you desire, I will give you another vineyard in its place. He said, I will not give you my vineyard.
Jezebel his wife said to him, You now exercise kingship over Israel? Arise, eat bread, and let your heart be good. I will give you vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.
She wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent letters to elders and nobles living in Naboth's city.
She wrote in letters: Proclaim a fast and seat Naboth at head of people.
Seat two worthless men before him, and let them testify against him, saying, You cursed Divine and king. Then take him out and stone him so he dies.
Men of his city—the elders and nobles living in his city—did as Jezebel sent to them, according to what was written in letters she sent.
They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at head of people.
Two worthless men came, sat before him, and testified against Naboth before people: Naboth cursed Divine and king. They took him outside city, stoned him with stones, and he died.
They sent to Jezebel, saying, Naboth was stoned and is dead.
When Jezebel heard Naboth was stoned and dead, she said to Ahab, Arise, possess vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver, for Naboth is not alive but dead.
When Ahab heard Naboth was dead, Ahab arose to go down to vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to possess it.
Word of YHWH came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:
Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Look, he is in vineyard of Naboth, where he went down to possess it.
Speak to him: Thus says YHWH, Have you murdered and also possessed? Then say: Thus says YHWH, In place where dogs licked blood of Naboth, dogs shall lick your blood—also yours.
Ahab said to Elijah, Have you found me, my enemy? He said, I found you, because you sold yourself to do evil in eyes of YHWH.
Look, I am bringing evil upon you, sweeping away after you, and cutting off from Ahab every male—literally, one who urinates against wall—both restrained and abandoned in Israel.
I will make your house like house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of provocation with which you provoked me and made Israel sin.
Also concerning Jezebel YHWH spoke: Dogs shall eat Jezebel by wall/rampart of Jezreel.
One belonging to Ahab who dies in city dogs shall eat, and one who dies in field birds of heavens shall eat.
Surely there was none like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil in eyes of YHWH, whom Jezebel his wife incited.
He acted very abominably by walking after idols according to all Amorites did, whom YHWH dispossessed before children of Israel.
When Ahab heard these words, he tore his garments, placed sackcloth upon his flesh, fasted, lay in sackcloth, and walked softly.
Word of YHWH came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:
Have you seen how Ahab humbled himself before me? Because he humbled himself before me, I will not bring evil in his days; in days of his son I will bring evil upon his house.

translation_notes: Naboth's vineyard is ancestral inheritance, not merely a commodity. His refusal protects family, identity, livelihood, and covenant land obligations against royal acquisition.
Ahab offers exchange or payment but responds to a lawful refusal with entitlement and withdrawal. A ruler's disappointment does not create a public need or right of seizure.

Jezebel uses Ahab's name, seal, local elders, a public fast, false witnesses, religious accusation, and execution law to manufacture legitimacy for murder. This is coordinated state and judicial corruption.
The local elders and nobles comply. Responsibility extends beyond Jezebel to every official, witness, executioner, beneficiary, and Ahab himself, who knowingly takes the land after Naboth's death.
The charge joins offense against Divine and king, showing how religion can be weaponized to protect political power and silence landholders.
Naboth is stoned outside the city. Capital punishment and public participation do not make false judgment just.
Elijah's question—Have you murdered and also possessed?—binds land seizure to the killing that made it possible. Restitution is conspicuously absent from Ahab's response.
Jezebel is individually accountable, but the chapter's phrasing has fueled misogynistic and xenophobic scapegoating. Ahab is king, seal owner, beneficiary, and active possessor.
Threats of dogs eating bodies and destruction of descendants are corpse desecration and collective punishment, not ethical justice.
Ahab's humility delays judgment to his son's generation. Repentance without restitution to Naboth's family remains incomplete, and transferring punishment to children is unjust.
safety_note: Do not use law, fasting, religious accusation, forged authority, or public consensus to seize land or silence dissent. Do not scapegoat Jezebel while excusing Ahab and collaborating officials. Center Naboth's land rights, due process, restitution, and protection from state violence; children must not inherit punishment.
